subject: Demo recap: streaming partial-output investigation + proposed benchmarks / next steps

Subject: Demo recap: streaming partial-output investigation + proposed benchmarks / next steps

Hi Alex / Emily —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we don't lose momentum:

What we saw
- During the live demo you shared, certain user prompts produced "partial" answers in the UI (truncated sentences, abrupt stop before closing bracket in structured output). This happened intermittently and looked correlated with longer context windows / multimodal snippets in the prompt.
- You also reported some messages that never hit your client-side stop sequence (you expect a trailing "\n" or "<END>"), and occasional P95 latency spikes that make streaming UX feel jittery.

Hypothesis / immediate asks
1) Stop sequence mismatch: client-side stop token vs model tokenization differences can cause streams to continue producing until an unrelated token matches the stop sequence.
2) Early KV cache flush or premature chunking: for sessions with large past context we may be hitting an execution path that flushes partial outputs to the stream.
3) Tokenization/regeneration edge-case for your JSON-like structured responses.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
- Give us a sample of ~200 transcripts (anonymized) or the CSV you mentioned; we can run a 48-hour targeted eval across 3 model candidates and reproduce the failures. (I attached a sample prompt set: streaming_prompt_set_v1.jsonl).
- We'll run: rwd-13b-8k-fp16, rwd-7b-16k-q4, and a higher-latency fallback (rwd-30b-16k) to surface regression differences.
- Deliverables: short repro playbook, per-model failure-rate and P95 streaming latency table, and recommended config (stop token mapping + client chunking suggestions).

Timing: can you share the CSV by end of day Tuesday (Nov 24)? We can run the first pass Wednesday/Thursday and sync late next week.

Attachments: streaming_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (prompt set TF/JSONL), benchmark_plan_v2.pdf (test matrix)

Thanks —
Marissa

- We'll extract the transcripts and strip PHI; Emily and I will gate the anonymized CSV (should be ready by Tue EOD). File will be named medicallabs_sample_transcripts.csv.
- Our desired UX SLOs: P50 < 60ms, P95 < 150ms for token stream delivery in our US region. Anything over that on spikes is noticeable to clinicians.
- For stop sequences: our front-end currently sends a literal "<END>" marker and also expects any trailing newline to be considered termination. We've seen some outputs that continued after the marker and then emitted a partial sentence.

Also attaching a 30s recording of the session where it happened (repro_steps-recording.mp3). Let us know if you want a remote screen-share to reproduce live.

> Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we don't lose momentum:

Alex / Emily —

Thanks for the artifacts. I pulled the recording and skimmed the CSV; a couple quick technical hypotheses and the test plan we intend to run (we'll execute once you confirm the CSV).

Technical hypotheses (concise)
- Stop-token alignment: client sends literal string markers that may map to multi-token sequences in the model tokenizer; the stream only signals a stop when the decoded token boundary matches, so partial tokens may leak into the stream. Mapping stop sequences to model token IDs (or using a dedicated post-process filter) should fix most cases.
- Streaming flush behavior: for large prefix contexts we hit a different execution kernel that flushes incomplete decoder output on buffer flush. This can look like truncated sentences mid-phrase. We'll instrument that path.
- Backpressure / chunking: client chunk size + network jitter can make certain tokens appear delayed and reassembled incorrectly on the UI, creating a perception of "coherence drop".

Planned test matrix (we'll run these in parallel):
1) Repro run against the three candidates Marissa listed with your transcripts. Each job will produce per-prompt pass/fail, P50/P95 token latency, and stop-token alignment failure rate.
2) Incremental tests toggling: (a) enforce stop via model-side post-filtering, (b) reduce client chunk size to 256 bytes, (c) force same tokenizer settings across client and model.
3) If we see model-specific regression, we will snapshot the exact commit + kernel used and recommend a pin (or fallback) with an explanation.

Deliverables we'll upload to the Drive link I shared and include a short executive summary for your CTO. If the tests reproduce reliably we'll propose a short SOW (2-week focused eval + patching) or a standing Dedicated pilot depending on scope.

Next actions from Alex: confirm CSV delivery and any additional sample prompts you want prioritized.

Attachments referenced: medicallabs_sample_transcripts.csv (pending), benchmark_plan_v2.pdf

Thanks,
